## Reviewer evidence

The reviewers for `#169`–`#159` were **real, freshly spawned, independent subagents** running on the
Babel-native OpenCode Go harness. They were bound to an exact base/head, candidate digest and
diff-numstat digest, and they returned APPROVE/BLOCK with reproducible counterexamples. The V3
isolation booleans (`candidate_write`, `github_mutation`, `merge`, `controller_state_access` all
false) are host/controller attestations recorded in the schema and authenticated by the live
owner-comment provenance — schema-enforced, but not an independent cryptographic sandbox proof. The
orchestrator that spawned the reviewers did not modify a candidate after freezing it, and reviewers had
no merge authority. Genuine final-round results were serialized into the V3 `host_review_handoff_v3`
schema and published as the owner-authenticated GitHub comment consumed by the trusted control plane.
No approval was hand-authored.

**BLOCK handling.** Round-1 BLOCK verdicts were genuine host reviewer executions retained in host
state. They were intentionally **not** published as V3 handoffs: `Select-AgentHostReviewBundle` binds
each handoff to an exact base/head and selects the newest comment whose SHAs match, so a round-1 BLOCK
is bound to the pre-repair head and is simply not selected for the repaired head. Publishing only the
certified final round keeps the published artifact equal to the merged candidate. The round-1 execution
IDs below are host records, not GitHub artifacts. Every repair produced a new candidate SHA, and each
new candidate was certified by a new reviewer context (no BLOCK was converted to APPROVE without a
candidate change).

`#170` is the exception: it reused pre-existing exact-candidate V3 evidence that was published by the
prior campaign. Its reviewers recorded an external provider (`google-antigravity`, `gemini-2.5-flash`,
`agent_kind = independent_subagent`, `adapter_id = subagent-adapter-v3`), which is allowed by the V3
schema for a non-Babel adapter. The runtime-attribution paragraph below therefore applies only to the
reviewers spawned in this continuation.

### Genuine defects caught by review and repaired

- **#169** — trailing-dot/percent-encoded FQDN bypass of the inference-host blocklist, a missing
  registered provider, and a contract test that did not pin the `--import` bootstrap. Repaired:
  hostname normalization, expanded blocklist, load-time bootstrap pin, fail-loud register bootstrap.
- **#167** — candidate A's guard only fired when the caller passed *no* model, but the production
  `CompactionManager` always passes an ambient-derived model, so a Qwen/deepseek id could still be
  dispatched to `api.anthropic.com`. Candidate C additionally let an OpenRouter credential reach the
  Anthropic endpoint through the explicit-base branch. Candidate D enforces endpoint↔model coherence
  **and** endpoint↔credential matching (including explicit `BABEL_COMPACTION_API_BASE`), with a
  wire-level test capturing URL plus auth header.
- **#166** — candidate A only widened the resolver; the anti-thrash post-write window still killed
  mutating runs 3–8 minutes after the first write, and the flag was stripped from child environments.
  Candidate B skips the post-write wall shrink only under the explicitly authorized profile and
  forwards `BABEL_CHAT_LONG_TASK` / `BABEL_CHAT_MAX_WALL_MS` through `getSafeEnv`.
- **#159** — candidate A resolved the clone-local fallback to the clone's *grandparent* instead of the
  historical parent, and validated the clone directory name even when unused, breaking clones with
  spaces. Candidate B restores the parent fallback and scopes the name validation.

### Reviewer runtime attribution (continuation reviewers only)

The subagent reviewers for `#169`–`#159` executed on the Babel-native OpenCode Go harness
(`observed_provider = opencode-go`, `observed_model = deepseek-v4.1-flash`), recorded as
`model_attribution = observed`. The V3 schema classifies `opencode-go` as the `babel` agent kind, so
they are recorded as `agent_kind = babel` with `adapter_id = opencode-go-subagent-adapter-v3`; the
mechanism is explicit in the adapter id. `runtime_version` is a **host-asserted** deterministic
digest computed by the orchestrator over the trusted base-rooted review-gate code
(`scripts/agent-pr-gate-common.psm1` + `scripts/agent-review-evidence.ps1`); the in-repo schema only
requires a 64-hex value, so the derivation is not independently reproducible from the repository.
`#170`'s reused evidence records the prior campaign's external provider instead.

Review token telemetry was only partially observable from the host runtime; observed values were used
where available and **unknown values were left unknown — no zero was synthesized**. Complete
per-execution totals remain unknown.

## Integrated canary (bounded, no live inference)

Scenario (host runner on final main `18fd3f5`): build an M/B/I experiment contract V3 → run a real
bounded Babel benchmark harness with the mock provider → run a deterministic verifier subprocess →
write lifecycle records through the bounded TUI observation sink → ingest a run directory through
canonical Run Intelligence → compare the contract cells → verify identity/telemetry → clean up. The
canary writes lifecycle records directly through the sink's public writer
(`appendTuiLifecycleEvent`); the kinds it chose are canary-defined records, not necessarily the
engine-translated event kinds that the observe session forwards in normal use.

Result — all steps passed:

| Step | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Experiment contract creation | `preflightV3 = []`, stable `contractDigest = c8556671…c8e285` |
| Babel execution (mock provider) | benchmark harness exit 0, `provider = mock`, 15 results |
| Deterministic verifier | `node` verifier exit 0 on the fixture |
| Lifecycle capture | 3 records written and reloaded via the observation sink: `model_started`, `verifier_result`, `terminal_status` |
| Outcome/receipt ingestion | Run Intelligence receipt `receipt_dde6bc3a…`, 7 entities, coverage/inventory non-empty |
| Outcome comparison | `EXPERIMENT_VERDICT = TIE`, `VALIDITY = VALID` (`M_vs_B`, `B_vs_I` VALID) |
| Run identity + telemetry survival | run id/`revision` bound to the contract; lifecycle records reloaded |
| No unauthorized inference | 0 provider keys present, guard opt-in absent, mock provider only |
| Cleanup | temp workspace removed |

Failures encountered: none. The canary was run twice (mid-campaign on `1727a77` and finally on
`18fd3f5`) and passed both times. It is a bounded smoke test, not an independent reproduction of the
removed workspace; its evidence is the host run recorded here. The concrete values above
(`contractDigest`, receipt id, verdict, counts) are **host-observed and not independently reproducible
from the repository** — no canary artifact was retained in `main`.

## Remaining risks

**Real blockers:** none identified. The controlled Astra benchmark campaign can begin.

**Known limitations (documented, non-blocking):**

- **#165 production posture.** The provider tool-cycle invariant enforces in dev/CI by default but is
  `shadow` under `NODE_ENV=production`, matching the pre-existing C1 contract; production relies on
  provider-side rejection. Structural malformation is blocked before dispatch outside production.
- **#169 coverage boundary.** The ambient-inference guard wraps `globalThis.fetch` only; direct
  `node:http(s)`, SDK-internal non-global fetch (Groq), `wss:` and provider CLI subprocesses are not
  intercepted. The module header documents this.
- **#166 cost interaction.** The post-write/critic repair cost window still caps extra spend after the
  first write; a multi-hour run at default cost can be cost-killed first. The wall profile is
  independent of cost by design.
- **#167 custom endpoint.** With an operator-set `BABEL_COMPACTION_API_BASE` on an unrecognized host,
  credential selection falls back to legacy priority; endpoint classification uses substring matching.
  Both are pre-existing and operator-controlled.
- **#168 schema.** The daemon result artifact is now `schema_version: 2` with no runtime migration
  gate; there is currently no in-repo reader beyond tests.
- **#159 CI wiring.** The new central-storage test is not referenced by a workflow; a reparse point in
  a junctioned Windows workspace now fails closed (possible false positive).

**Deferred improvements:** duplicate-declaration and whitespace-id detection in the tool-cycle
validator; a repair path for resuming a partially-answered tool batch; wiring the central-worktree
test into CI; anchoring endpoint classification to parsed hostnames; widening `maxTurns`/cost under an
authorized long-task profile; engine-level emission of `wallBudget`.

**Experiment questions for Astra:** whether the long-task profile plus an explicit cost ceiling
actually sustains the intended multi-hour runs end to end; whether the provider protocol invariant
should become enforce-by-default in production; and how compaction provider/model routing behaves
under the mix of real Astra providers and ambient credentials.
